Q0m.title: Quantum ground-state maximum
Q0m.scenario: Confine a quantum particle to an infinite triangular well. Select the most probable location in the positive ground state.
Q0m.algorithm: Use quadratic FEM eigenpairs and coordinate-weighted mass matrices. Search stationary points within quadratic elements for the maximum, then refine its location.
Q0m.attract: A candidate negative finite response appears only after substantial refinement; its small magnitude and maximum-location sensitivity leave the rigorous conclusion open.
Q0m.location: Unique interior maximum: log-concavity, interior analyticity and zero boundary trace give the line-restriction argument in Section 2. The Hardy/disk bound applies to expectations, not this maximum.
Q0m.extra: At equilateral the center is unambiguous. The thin correction has the ground-mode Airy scale.

Q0.title: Quantum ground-state expectation

Q0.algorithm: Use quadratic FEM eigenpairs and coordinate-weighted mass matrices. Normalize in the mass matrix, integrate the first moment, and retain the adjacent spectral gaps.
Q0.attract: Refined finite-displacement computations have stable negative signs. These are numerical counterexamples, not interval-certified continuum statements.
Q0.location: Every nonzero state mean is strictly interior; $d_i(Q_j)\geq r/(2\zeta_j)$ gives the stronger inner-parallel-triangle bound.
Q0.extra: At equilateral the center is unambiguous. The thin correction has the ground-mode Airy scale.

Pgrav.extra: This is the linear clamped model. Rotationally free boundaries, large deflections and nonuniform thickness change the problem.
